title: bee-core D9 lock protocol port + node-rust interop conformance
action: Port the D9 lock-file protocol into bee-core (crate member scaffolded by rust-port-1; fsutil primitives come from rust-port-5): lock path scheme (sanitized name + sha256 first 8 hex under .bee/locks/), body {pid,session,ts,token}, STALE_MS 30s / HARD_STALE_MS 1h, pid-liveness probe takeover verified by pid+token+ts identity, transient-FS retry policy, hooks-never-wait try-once mode (maxAttempts 1), contention.jsonl fail-open telemetry. SCOPE NOTE (validation decision): the sharded lease store (lease-store.mjs — batch acquire, hash-sorted order, rollback, workspace_id scoping) is DEFERRED to Slice 3 where its consumers (claims/reservations) are ported; Slice 0 D9 proof covers the lock-file protocol plan.md names. Conformance tests MUST include cross-runtime interop: a node child process driving the real .bee/bin/lib/lock.mjs (exports are root-parameterized: locksDir(root), acquireStoreLockOnceSync(root, name) returning {acquired, release}/{acquired, holder} — proven by spike .bee/spikes/rust-port/lock_probe.mjs) holding while rust contends, and the reverse; staleness takeover; a two-simultaneous-holders negative test that fails red on protocol violation. The node driver is a FILE under crates/bee-core/tests/ (never `node -e` — the internals-reach guard denies inline evals importing bin/lib), its path to lock.mjs resolved by walking ancestors from CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR. Staleness is controlled by writing a backdated `ts` into the lock body — never by sleeping.

truths: rust contender never acquires while a live node holder exists (and vice versa)
stale-holder takeover succeeds only via liveness-probe/hard-stale path with pid+token+ts identity verification
two-simultaneous-holders negative test fails red when the protocol is deliberately violated

artifacts.substantive: lock module + interop test suite (file-based node driver) covering hold, deny, takeover, try-once, contention log

key_links: interop tests execute the real .bee/bin/lib/lock.mjs in a node child, not a reimplementation
prohibitions: No edits to .bee/bin/lib/lock.mjs (mjs frozen per D1)
Interop tests never operate on the repo's live .bee/ store — every node driver call receives a per-test temp root as the lock.mjs root argument
No sleep-based staleness tests — backdated ts only
No edits to crates/Cargo.toml (members final per rust-port-1)

trace.outcome: D9 lock protocol ported to bee-core (crates/bee-core/src/lock.rs): path scheme (sanitized name + sha256 first-8-hex under .bee/locks/), body {pid,session,ts,token} O_EXCL, STALE_MS 30s/HARD_STALE_MS 1h with libc kill(0) pid-liveness probe, rename-based takeover verified by pid+token+ts identity before AND after the rename (settle/restore/never-clobber branches), transient-FS retry (15x20ms EBUSY/EPERM/ENOTEMPTY/EMFILE/ENFILE), hooks-never-wait try-once (LockOptions::try_once, max_attempts 1), fail-open contention.jsonl telemetry with the C3 schema. Cross-runtime conformance: 11 interop tests drive the REAL .bee/bin/lib/lock.mjs in node children via the file-based tests/support/lock_driver.mjs (path resolved by CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR ancestor walk) on per-test temp roots — live node holder denies rust and vice versa, node reads rust bodies and reverse, dead-pid stale takeover both directions, live-holder-below-ceiling never stolen, hard-ceiling steal with foreign-release staying scoped, two-simultaneous-holders detector proven to fail red on a deliberate unlink violation, try-once never waits, telemetry schema + fail-open. Plus 10 unit tests (identity-JS-semantics table, settle branch table, corrupt-stale-never-stolen, ISO-8601 node oracle, transient-retry budget). Staleness via backdated body ts + mtime, never sleep. Deps added to bee-core only: sha2, getrandom, libc(unix). Lease store deferred to Slice 3 per validation decision W3.
deviations: fsutil.rs: js_trim visibility widened to pub(crate) — the lock module session-id env chain and JS Number() coercion need ECMAScript trim semantics (FEFF included); no behavior change to fsutil itself

lock_driver.mjs hold op: explicit process.exit(0) after release ack — a flowing stdin listener otherwise keeps the node event loop alive and the Rust child.wait() hangs forever (found during first test run)
